analysis: The code snippet uses Float.parseFloat in two places: under 'AlphaTestFalloff' with split[1], and under 'PolyOffset' with split[1] and split[2]. The split array is derived from statement.getLine().split(whitespacePattern). split() never returns null and elements are never null, so the argument to parseFloat is never null. Thus, NullPointerException is avoided. However, there is no validation of the string content before parsing. If split[1] or split[2] is not a valid float representation (e.g., empty string, non-numeric characters), NumberFormatException will be thrown. Therefore, NumberFormatException is not avoided.
remark: NumberFormatException can be triggered if split[1] (in AlphaTestFalloff) or split[1] or split[2] (in PolyOffset) is not a parsable float. Examples include empty strings (e.g., line has trailing whitespace causing split to produce an empty token) or non-numeric strings like 'abc'.
